name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
December 3, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:01 p.m. , on December 3, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on November 28, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Conference With Legal Counsel -- Anticipated Litigation. Based on existing facts and circumstances, the City Council/Successor Agency and PFA will confer with legal counsel and provide direction regarding (i) whether or not to initiate litigation pursuant to Section 54956.9(c) - one potential case, and (ii) significant exposure to litigation pursuant to Section 54956.9(b) - one potential case.
CS2.
Conference With Legal Counsel -- Anticipated Litigation. Based on existing facts and circumstances, the Successor Agency and Housing Authority will confer with legal counsel and provide direction regarding (i) whether or not to initiate litigation pursuant to Section 54956.9(c) - one potential case, and (ii) significant exposure to litigation pursuant to Section 54956.9(b) - one potential case.
CS3.
Labor Negotiations -- The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
CS4.
Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council addressed items CS1 and CS2. The Council received an update and provided general direction to staff but no reportable action occurred. Items CS3 and CS4 were not considered and will be continued to a future meeting.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Mayor's State of the City Address
The City Council and audience received the Mayor's State of the City address.
P2.
Administration of Oaths of Office
Francis K. Holtzman, Haya Sakadjian, and Larry Gilbert administered the Oath of Office to Cathy Schlicht and Alex Ury administered the Oath of Office to Frank Ury. City Clerk Karen Hamman presented Certificates of Election to Council Members Schlicht and Ury.
RECESS
At the hour of 6:42 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Dan Avery, M.V.: announced that there is a simple and inexpensive mesh barrier for preventing rattle snakes from entering a particular area. He suggested that the product may be useful at the proposed dog park.
Laura Johnson, M.V.: stated that she is concerned about the number of very serious accidents that have occurred on Vista Del Lago between Los Alisos and Marguerite Parkway due to excessive speeds and reckless driving. She asked the City Council to consider this matter in the near future.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: wished everyone a Merry Christmas and thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for the wonderful Santa's arrival and tree lighting event. She also encouraged residents to donate toys for the Jessie Rees Foundation NEGU Joy Jars. Mrs. Bucknum outlined an upcoming event at Saddleback College called "Election 2012 - How the Results will Affect Small Business" on December 7, from 2:00 to 5:00 p.m. and the Presbyterian Church of the Master's Christmas concert on Sunday, December 9 at 4:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular meeting of November 19, 2012, as presented.
3.
Claim Against the City - AIFNI Insurance Services as Subrogee of Lisa Bracken vs. City of Mission Viejo
Rejected claim.
4.
Official Results of the November 6, 2012 General Municipal Election
Adopted Resolution 12-67 Reciting the Fact That a General Municipal Election was Held on November 6, 2012, and Declaring the Results Thereof.
5.
Check Register Dated November 9, 2012 in the Amount of $1,126,113.26
Ratified the accompanying check register.
6.
Check Register Dated November 16, 2012 in the Amount of $846,090.31
Ratified the accompanying check register.
7.
Check Register Dated November 23, 2012 in the Amount of $2,712,109.91
Ratified the accompanying check register.
8.
Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2012
Received and filed.
9.
Annual Measure M-2 Expenditure Report for Fiscal Year Ended 6/30/12
Approved Resolution 12-68 Adopting the Measure M-2 Expenditure Report for the City of Mission Viejo.
10.
Cooperative Agreements for the Los Alisos Boulevard, Santa Margarita Parkway and Oso Parkway / Pacific Park Drive Traffic Signal Synchronization Programs (Project P)
(1) Approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-2-1994 with the Orange County Transportation Authority for the Santa Margarita Parkway Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P); (2) approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-2-1995 with the Orange County Transportation Authority for the Oso Parkway/Pacific Park Drive Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P); and (3) approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-2-1996 with the Orange County Transportation Authority for the Los Alisos Boulevard Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P).
PUBLIC HEARINGS
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
OLD BUSINESS
11.
Mission Viejo Dog Park - (CIP 313)
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
The following spoke in favor of a dog park at the proposed location: Avery Ackerman, M.V.; Walter Halagarda, M.V.; Linda Cooper, M.V.; Dan Avery, M.V.; Nancy Chontos, M.V.; Debbie Corwin, M.V.; Caroline Kruebbe, M.V.; Sharon Cody, M.V.; Jamie Beaudry, M.V.; Chris Nelson, M.V.; Ben Sellers, M.V.; Corissa Sellers, M.V.; Susan Sellers, M.V.; Nermine Marcos, M.V.; Daphne Ashbrook M.V.; Cari Cohn Morros, M.V.; Maribeth McFaul, M.V.; Eric Daniel Nichols, M.V.; Patricia Wise, M.V.; Elizabeth Mead, M.V.; Anna T. Boyce, M.V.; and Patti Bennett, M.V.
The following spoke in opposition to a dog park at the proposed location: Dale Sandore, M.V.; and Harry Lenczyk, M.V.
The following presented written comments in favor of a dog park: Stephanie Colby, M.V.; Anna Hepler, M.V.; and John and Arlene Spears, M.V.
The following presented written comments in opposition to the cost and/or location of the proposed dog park: G. Eric Brown, M.V.; Carol Schwimmer, M.V.; and Steven Schwimmer, M.V.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1) approve the bid specifications and plans and authorize staff to advertise for bids for the Mission Viejo Dog Park (CIP 313); (2) adopt Resolution 12-69 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget for Recognition of Park Development Fees and an Appropriation Related to Capital Improvement Project 313 Mission Viejo Dog Park; and (3) approve Amendment No. 3 to MCE Engineering Consultants in an amount not to exceed $28,350.00.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
ABSENT:
None
RECESS
At the hour of 8:58 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:09 p.m., with four City Council Members present. Council Member Schlicht returned to the dais at 9:11 p.m.
12.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented staff report.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she would like to see an item on a future agenda to review key learnings from this project.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and thirty-five (35) days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; (4) authorize the payment of the final retention of $428,139; thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion; (5) approve Change Order No. 11 to Western Alta Construction in the amount of $39,810; approve Change Order No. 2 to Petra Geotechnical Services in the amount of $5,268; and (6) adopt Resolution 12-70 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 budget for costs related to Capital Improvement Marguerite Tennis Center Project 501 for $59,642.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR'S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
13.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Council Member Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCFA Board of Directors.
14.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury stated that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA.
15.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that the San Joaquin Hills TCA Board meeting will be held later this week.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager's Report
16.
Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board
City Manager Wilberg presented the report and discussed the actions that the Oversight Board and Successor Agency took at special meetings earlier in the day. He also outlined staff's recent meeting with the State Department of Finance and he noted that the City should hear back from the DOF by December 15, 2012.
City Attorney's Report
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
17.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their events and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley congratulated Mayor Ury on his appointment to the OCTA Board of Directors. She also thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for the outstanding Santa's Arrival event which she attended with her three grandchildren. Santa's entrance on a fire truck is a highlight every year for the children in the community and she reminded residents that they can visit Santa in his workshop every Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. through December 19. Visits with Santa are free and parents can take their own pictures. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of December is caring and she wished everyone a Merry Christmas and a happy Hanukkah.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness outlined his attendance at the Feast of Lights at Saddleback College, a phenomenal Christmas extravaganza with a chorus of singers and a full orchestra. This was the twenty-third year and his third year attending. Council Member Leckness announced that he will be the tour guide on the Holly Trolley on Friday and Saturday, December 7 and 8. He invited residents to join in the tour of holiday lights and he wished a Merry Christmas to all.
Council Member Schlicht
18.
Cities Annual Report and City Treasurer's Monthly Report
Council Member Schlicht noted that her agenda report is simply for receipt and filing and was meant to inform the public of the City's financial data.
Council Member Schlicht thanked everyone for their support this election season; all the volunteers who put their lives on hold to help take her to victory and the voters for seeing past special influence money and re-electing her. She expressed her deep thanks for the trust that the voters put in her and she promised to continue to work hard, ask questions, and march forward with what she believes. Council Member Schlicht reminded residents that this is the last Council Meeting of the year and she wished everyone a happy Christmas and happy Hanukkah.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon noted that she would have been interested in hearing a report for item 18. She also outlined her attendance at the Santa's Arrival event which she attended with her three grandsons. She thanked Keith Rattay and stated that Mission Viejo is just drop-dead gorgeous at Christmas time. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon reminded residents that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee volunteers host and help Santa in his workshop every Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday night. She also reminded residents that the City is collecting toys for the Marines and for NEGU Joy Jars through December 14. She further shared the news that Mission Viejo's Blackhawks Elite Pony baseball team won a recent qualifier game and will compete next in the World Series Championship game in Colorado. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon thanked the Information Technology Department for their hard work in upgrading the library's computer system and she wish residents a very Merry Christmas, happy New Year, Happy Hanukkah, and a very blessed holiday season.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury thanked his colleagues for a very civil discourse on the dog park this evening. He stated that he too enjoyed the Santa's Arrival event and holding Council Member Kelley's grandson during the show. Mayor Ury indicated that he is very excited about his appointment to the OCTA Board of Directors which sets transportation policy for the entire County of Orange. He looks forward to conducting outreach in the community and to working on traffic matters, especially those issues that affect South County. Mr. Ury thanked his colleagues and staff for a wonderful year while he served as Mayor and he wished everyone a Merry Christmas, happy New Year and happy Hanukkah.
CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION
19.
Appointment of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem
City Clerk Karen Hamman asked the Council for nominations for Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to appoint Rhonda Reardon as Mayor for 2013.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint Trish Kelley as Mayor Pro Tem for 2013.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
ABSENT:
None
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 9:39 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, January 7, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of January 07, 2013
